mainTopic: Which חולין can become שלישי, and the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about whether one who eats impure food becomes as impure as the food
overview: The גמרא is looking for the case in the משנה where meat could become שלישי (third-degree impure). Ordinary חולין normally cannot become שלישי. It first suggests חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה, following רבי יהושע. It rejects this, because no one keeps meat at the level of תרומה. It settles on חולין kept at the purity level of קדשים, which can apply even to a חיה, because meat gets mixed up with meat. עולא then brings two views. His colleagues say the משנה does not follow רבי יהושע. עולא says it does, reading רבי יהושע as 'לא מיבעיא'. The colleagues turn out to be רבה בר בר חנה, who quotes רבי יוחנן's account of a debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about whether someone who eats impure food becomes as impure as the food. Each side brings a proof and the other rejects it. רבי יהושע then begins to explain that his rule about eating a שלישי applies only to תרומה, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggestion: the משנה is about חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה, following רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the משנה is talking about ordinary food that someone treats with the strictness of תרומה. It says this follows רבי יהושע, who holds that such food can become שלישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is about חולין that were prepared at the purity level of תרומה, and it follows רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the earlier question of how the משנה's meat could become third-degree impure. It suggests the משנה is about חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה, following רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal חולין cannot become שלישי, yet the משנה implies they can. רבי יהושע holds that חולין handled with the strictness of תרומה can become שלישי. If the משנה follows him, the problem is solved.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food
The purity level required for תרומה (the כהן's portion)
That were prepared according to (a higher purity standard)

steps.confusionAlert: The food here is still חולין. It is not real תרומה. The person simply chooses to guard it with the strictness of תרומה.

phrases.english: With regard to non-sacred food prepared at the purity level of teruma,
and following Rabbi Yehoshua?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question that came right before this section
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה, following רבי יהושע, who allows them to become שלישי

steps.title: Objection: nobody keeps meat at the purity level of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The משנה talks about meat, and the purity level of תרומה is never applied to meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so. The משנה speaks about meat, and if we were dealing with the purity level of תרומה, is there such a thing as meat at that level?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 1. The משנה is about meat, and meat has nothing to do with the purity level of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה comes only from produce that grows in the ground, never from meat. So no one would keep meat at the purity level of תרומה. The case in step 1 does not fit a משנה about slaughtered animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think so; that idea cannot be right
Meat
Is there such a thing? (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
since the mishna teaches about "meat,"
and if it is about teruma – is there meat?
phrases.notes: תרומה comes only from produce of the ground, so meat never has a תרומה purity level.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the משנה is about the purity level of תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with meat, and the purity level of תרומה only applies to produce

steps.title: The alternative of קדשים runs into a problem with חיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the purity level of קדשים instead. But the משנה also mentions a חיה (wild animal), and a חיה can never be brought as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what then, it is about the purity level of קדשים? But is there a חיה among קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: Since תרומה did not work, the גמרא considers the purity level of קדשים. It immediately raises a problem: the משנה includes a wild animal, and wild animals are never קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat does connect to קדשים, because animal קרבנות are meat. But the משנה lists בהמה, חיה and עוף together. Why would anyone keep a חיה at the purity level of קדשים if a חיה can never be a קרבן?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what then? (introduces the remaining option, often with a problem)
Holy sacrificial food
A wild, undomesticated animal (such as a deer)

phrases.english: Rather, what – with regard to sacrificial food?
phrases.notes: He means חולין kept at the purity level of קדשים.

phrases.english: Is there an undomesticated animal among sacrificial food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting תרומה, it considers קדשים and challenges that option
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה is about the purity level of קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה includes a חיה, which can never be a קרבן, so the purity level of קדשים seems irrelevant to it

steps.title: Meat gets mixed up with meat, but not with produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people do treat wild-animal meat at the purity level of קדשים, because one kind of meat can be confused with another. Meat is never confused with produce, so no one keeps meat at the level of תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat can be confused with meat, but meat cannot be confused with produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem with חיה. Someone might guard wild-animal meat at the purity level of קדשים because it can be mixed up with domestic-animal meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat from a חיה looks like meat from a בהמה, which can be a קרבן. So a person being careful with קדשים might treat all meat the same way. Produce looks nothing like meat, so the תרומה option still fails. The קדשים reading survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets confused or interchanged
Produce, fruits

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about חולין kept at the purity level of קדשים, not תרומה. That level applies even to a חיה, because meat gets confused with meat.

phrases.english: Meat is interchanged with meat,
phrases.notes: Wild-animal meat can be mistaken for domestic-animal meat, which can be a קרבן.

phrases.english: meat is not interchanged with produce.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a practical reason that extends the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חיה has no connection to קדשים, so the purity level of קדשים cannot apply to it
steps.terutzMaskana: Because meat gets confused with meat, people guard even חיה meat at the purity level of קדשים. Produce is never confused with meat.

steps.title: עולא's colleagues: the משנה is about קדשים and does not follow רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports what his colleagues said. The משנה is about חולין at the purity level of קדשים, and it is not in line with רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The colleagues say the משנה is about חולין prepared at the purity level of קדשים, and it does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings the view of his colleagues. They agree the case is the purity level of קדשים, but they say this does not match רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע spoke about חולין at the purity level of תרומה having שלישי. The colleagues read him as limiting this to the level of תרומה. Since the משנה is about the level of קדשים, they conclude it does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: The colleagues, fellow scholars
The purity level required for holy sacrificial food

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The colleagues say
it is about non-sacred food prepared at the purity level of sacrificial food,
and not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the קדשים conclusion and asks whose view it fits
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is about the purity level of קדשים and does not follow רבי יהושע

steps.title: עולא himself: it does follow רבי יהושע, read as 'לא מיבעיא'
steps.stepSummary: עולא disagrees with his colleagues. רבי יהושע mentioned תרומה only to teach a bigger point. Obviously the stricter level of קדשים brings שלישי, and even the level of תרומה does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say the משנה follows רבי יהושע, and he was speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that חולין at the purity level of קדשים, which is stricter, can become שלישי. Rather, even חולין at the purity level of תרומה can become שלישי.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives his own view. The משנה does follow רבי יהושע, because רבי יהושע picked the easier case of תרומה to show that even it brings שלישי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The colleagues read רבי יהושע as limiting שלישי to the level of תרומה. עולא reads him the opposite way: קדשים is stricter than תרומה, so if the level of תרומה brings שלישי, the level of קדשים surely does. This way the משנה about the level of קדשים fits רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (start with the obvious case, then add the bigger one)
Third-degree impurity
Which is more stringent

steps.whatToRemember: Two readings of רבי יהושע. The colleagues say only the level of תרומה brings שלישי, so the משנה is not like him. עולא says 'all the more so' the level of קדשים, so the משנה is like him.
steps.confusionAlert: In a 'לא מיבעיא' statement, the case actually spoken about (תרומה) is the surprising, bigger point. The stricter case (קדשים) is the obvious one that 'goes without saying.'

phrases.english: And I say it is Rabbi Yehoshua,
and he is speaking in the style of "it is not necessary":

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת קֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: it is not necessary to say non-sacred food prepared at the purity level of sacrificial food,
which is stringent, that it has third-degree impurity,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: but even non-sacred food prepared at the purity level of teruma
also has third-degree impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the colleagues' reading of רבי יהושע in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, because his statement about the level of תרומה means 'all the more so' the level of קדשים brings שלישי

steps.title: Who were the colleagues?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'colleagues' were whose view עולא reported.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick identity question: who were the 'colleagues' עולא mentioned in Step 5? This sets up the next step, which names them and quotes their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 עולא reported that his colleagues said the משנה is not in line with רבי יהושע. Before going on, the גמרא wants to know who said this, so we can see the reasoning behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: Who are the colleagues?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who the colleagues were that עולא quoted in Step 5 and then argued against in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'colleagues' in עולא's statement.

steps.title: It is רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The colleague is רבה בר בר חנה. He quotes רבי יוחנן, who describes how רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע answered each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבה בר בר חנה. As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What did רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע answer each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the colleague is רבה בר בר חנה. It then begins quoting his report of a debate, so this line sets up the argument that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debate is about a person who eats impure food. רבי אליעזר says the eater gets the same level of impurity as the food. רבי יהושע says the eater usually becomes a שני. The next steps lay out each side's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: They answered back, replied
To each other

phrases.english: It is רבה בר בר חנה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said:
What did רבי אליעזר
and רבי יהושע answer each other?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 and opens the quoted debate.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The colleague is רבה בר בר חנה, who reports רבי יוחנן's account of the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the eater can be stricter than the food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר proves from נבלת עוף טהור that the eater can be more impure than the food. So the eater should be at least as impure as the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to רבי יהושע: We found that the eater can be stricter than the food. The carcass of a kosher bird does not make you impure from outside contact, but eating it makes your clothes impure while it is in your throat. So how can we not treat the eater like the food?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings a proof for his view. He points to a case where eating something makes a person more impure than touching it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching a נבלת עוף טהור does nothing. Swallowing it makes the person impure, and even his clothes. If eating can make someone more impure than the food itself, then the eater should certainly be at least equal to the food.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
The throat, the place of swallowing
The person who eats
The food itself

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר said to רבי יהושע:
We found the eater stricter than the food,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ נִבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר בַּחוּץ – לֹא מְטַמֵּא,
phrases.english: since the carcass of a kosher bird, outside the body, does not make impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ אוֹכְלָהּ מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה,
phrases.english: while one who eats it makes clothes impure while it is in the throat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָנוּ הֵיאַךְ לֹא נַעֲשֶׂה אוֹכֵל כַּמַּאֲכָל?
phrases.english: so how should we not make the eater like the food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first argument in the quoted debate.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that the eater takes on the same impurity level as the food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נבלת עוף טהור, which makes a person impure only through eating.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the bird case is a one-time exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the proof, because the rule of נבלת עוף טהור is a חידוש and cannot be used to learn other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע: We do not learn from the carcass of a kosher bird, because it is a special new rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back on רבי אליעזר's proof. He says the bird case is unusual and cannot teach us anything about other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חידוש is a rule that goes against the normal pattern, so you cannot build a general principle on it. That leaves רבי אליעזר's proof without support.

keyTerms.meaning: A special, unusual rule that cannot be used to learn other cases
We learn, we derive

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע answered:

phrases.aramaic: מִנִּבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר לָא גָּמְרִינַן, דְּחִידּוּשׁ הוּא.
phrases.english: We do not learn from the carcass of a kosher bird, because it is a special new rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנִּבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר לָא גָּמְרִינַן, דְּחִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from נבלת עוף טהור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source is a חידוש, so other cases cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the food is stricter than the eater
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע brings a counter-proof. Food becomes impure at a כביצה, but an eater becomes impure only after a חצי פרס, so the eater should not be treated like the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we found that the food is stricter than the eater. Food is impure at the size of an egg, but the eater does not become impure until he eats half of a half-loaf. So how can we treat the eater like the food?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע brings his own proof, which points the other way: the food is stricter than the person who eats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can carry impurity at a small amount, a כביצה. An eater becomes impure only after a larger amount, a חצי פרס. Since the eater is treated more leniently, רבי יהושע argues he should not get the food's full level of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg-sized amount, the size at which food can carry impurity
Half of a half-loaf, a larger amount than an egg

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַמַּאֲכָל חָמוּר מִן הָאוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: Rather, we found that the food is stricter than the eater,
since food is impure at the size of an egg,
but the eater is not impure until he eats half of a half-loaf,
so how should we make the eater like the food?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַמַּאֲכָל חָמוּר מִן הָאוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי אליעזר's proof, רבי יהושע brings his own proof for the opposite view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's view that the eater is not equal to the food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The different amounts: כביצה for food and חצי פרס for an eater.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: amounts do not teach levels of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the proof, because we cannot learn how strict an impurity is from the amounts the הלכה requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר: We do not learn about impurity from required amounts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר pushes back on רבי יהושע's proof. Comparing amounts tells us nothing about how strong an impurity is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיעור, a required amount, is a separate question from the level of טומאה. A bigger required amount does not mean a weaker impurity, so רבי יהושע's comparison does not prove his point.

keyTerms.meaning: Required amounts or sizes set by הלכה
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר answered:
We do not learn about impurity from amounts,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהושע's counter-proof from Step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Required amounts are a separate question from the level of impurity, so one cannot be learned from the other.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: your own view does not hold together
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds that רבי יהושע's view seems to contradict itself. Eating a ראשון makes the eater a שני, which makes sense. But why should eating a שני also make the eater a שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, by your own words: when you say eating a ראשון makes the eater a שני, that is fine. But why should eating a שני make him a שני?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds a second attack, this time from inside רבי יהושע's own view. He says one part of that view does not fit his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eater is weaker than the food, as רבי יהושע argued, then eating a ראשון should make him a שני. That part works. But by the same reasoning, eating a שני should make him only a שלישי, so why is he a שני?

keyTerms.meaning: First-degree impurity
Second-degree impurity
And furthermore, which brings an extra argument

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the eater is as impure as the food (proof: נבלת עוף טהור). רבי יהושע: the eater is a שני (proof: כביצה vs. חצי פרס). Each side rejects the other's proof, and רבי אליעזר also claims רבי יהושע's view contradicts itself.
steps.confusionAlert: Read 'שני שני' as 'eating a שני makes the eater a שני.' It is not just the word repeated: the first שני is the food and the second שני is the eater.

phrases.english: And furthermore, by your words, what you say

phrases.aramaic: עַל רִאשׁוֹן שֵׁנִי – יָפֶה אַתָּה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: about a ראשון making the eater a שני, you say well,
but a שני making the eater a שני, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, internal challenge after rejecting the proof from amounts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's rule that eating a שני makes the eater a שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the eater is weaker than the food, eating a שני should make him only a שלישי, so ruling that he is a שני contradicts רבי יהושע's own reasoning.

steps.title: רבי יהושע finds a case of a second level making a second level
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that we do find a שני making something else a שני, when liquids are involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We find that a second-level impure item makes something else second level, through liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר's question from Step 13. He points to a known case where a שני passes on the same level, שני, to something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר asked how a שני can make the eater a שני, since normally impurity goes down one level each time it passes on. רבי יהושע answers that this already happens elsewhere. A שני touches liquid, the liquid touches food, and that food ends up a שני. So a שני producing a שני is not a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: We find; a precedent already exists
Liquids, which follow special rules for receiving impurity
By means of, through

phrases.english: He said to him: We have found
that a second-level item makes something second level
phrases.notes: He means: in the end, the food touched by the liquid is a שני, the same level as the item we started with.

phrases.english: by means of liquids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁנִי עוֹשֶׂה שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 about a שני making the eater a שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precedent: the same pattern already exists elsewhere in the laws of טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שני can never produce another שני, so רבי יהושע's view is inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through liquids, a שני does end up producing a שני, so his view has a parallel.

steps.title: Liquids become first level, so the case is not a real parallel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the liquids case. Liquids that touch a שני become a תחילה, so it is really a first level making a second level.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But liquids are also a first level, as we learned: Anything that disqualifies תרומה makes liquids become first level, except for a טבול יום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר rejects רבי יהושע's example. He quotes a משנה showing that the liquids themselves become first-level impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids have a special rule. Anything that disqualifies תרומה (a שני) makes liquids a תחילה, which is a higher level than the שני that touched them. So when that liquid makes food a שני, it is a normal ראשון making a שני, not a שני making a שני. The only exception is a טבול יום, whose touch does not make liquids a תחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a pushback)
First level of impurity, the same as a ראשון
Something that disqualifies תרומה, meaning a שני
A person who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to be fully pure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think liquids simply drop one level like everything else. The rule here is the opposite: a שני touching liquid makes the liquid a ראשון, which is a higher level.

phrases.english: He said to him: But the liquids
are also first level,
as we learned: Anything that disqualifies תרומה
phrases.notes: This quote is from משנה פרה 8:7.

phrases.english: makes liquids impure to become first level,
except for a טבול יום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וְהָא מַשְׁקִין נָמֵי תְּחִלָּה הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the precedent brought in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the liquids example as a parallel. It does not yet decide the main argument.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the liquids case the liquid becomes a תחילה, so it is a ראשון making a שני, not a שני making a שני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה פרה 8:7: כל הפוסל בתרומה מטמא משקין להיות תחלה, חוץ מטבול יום.

steps.title: Why should eating a third level make someone second level?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds a second question: according to רבי יהושע, why does eating a שלישי make the eater a שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: a third level makes a second level, why?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks another question against רבי יהושע's view. This time the question is about eating a שלישי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 asked why a שני can make the eater a שני. Now the problem is even bigger. In רבי יהושע's view, eating a שלישי can make the eater a שני. That means the eater goes up a level, which seems even harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?

phrases.english: And furthermore, a third level making a second level, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger version of the challenge from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that eating a שלישי makes the eater a שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impurity normally goes down a level as it passes on. Here the eater would end up higher than the food he ate.

steps.title: רבי יהושע limits his ruling to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע begins to answer: he only said this in connection with תרומה, because of the nature of its purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I too only said this regarding תרומה, whose purity...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע starts to answer the question about the שלישי. He explains that his ruling only applies in a narrow case connected to תרומה. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending this as a general rule, רבי יהושע narrows it. The case he meant is a שלישי of חולין prepared at the purity level of תרומה, the same case raised in step 1. The reason itself ("whose purity...") continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: I too; I also agree that it is limited
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept pure
Purity; here, the purity standard of תרומה

phrases.english: He said to him: I too
only said it regarding תרומה,
whose purity
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limitation: the ruling applies only in a specific case tied to תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating a שלישי makes the eater a שני as a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is limited to a case involving תרומה. The full reason continues on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is likely why the גמרא named רבה בר בר חנה as the source of עולא's colleagues' view (Step 8). In his report, רבי יהושע ties his rule to תרומה. That fits the colleagues' reading in Step 5: רבי יהושע's ruling about שלישי is limited to the purity level of תרומה and does not cover קדשים. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
